title: Wonunke (Westhampton)
summary: Wonunke is a Westhampton placename for necks of land east of Beaver Dam River, later appearing in Great and Little Wonunk forms.
introduction_content: Wonunke names a neck of land at West Hampton in Southampton town. Recorded forms include Great Wonunk, Little Wonunk, Ononke, Onunk, Wonunk, Wononck, Wonnonch, Wononke, Wonock, Onuck, and Onach.
history_content: The name belongs to the necks east of Beaver Dam River, also known as Apocuck Creek, where coves from the bay shaped the shoreline. Southampton records preserve several spellings across the late seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as "the bend," referring to a bend of land or water.

Why Place Names Matter

“Beyond the practical function they serve, Indigenous place names recount stories of the land in a unique way and provide valuable cultural and historical perspectives.”

— Translation Bureau, Government of Canada, Indigenous geographical names and the power they hold (2019), Language Portal of Canada blog, section “The moose that jumped over the rapids”

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
preservation_content: Wonunke connects modern Westhampton shoreline geography with older Southampton records and Indigenous-language place naming. The historic neck boundaries remain uncertain.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement in Westhampton east of Beaver Dam River/Apocuck Creek. Coordinates are approximate and not exact historic neck boundaries.
